checks.finding: All fourteen REQ-001..014 entries state observable, file/line-anchored obligations (schema fields, ownership digests, promotion evidence fields, rollback approval arithmetic, CI/OS matrix) that a fixture or resolver can measure. No requirement is stated only as intent.

REQ-003 (requirements.md:56-58) names four distinct A3-supplied checks the Context must pass: 'overlap, unowned-path, reverse-coverage, and ownership-digest checks'. AC-005/AC-006 (requirements.md:183-184; acceptance-tests.md:11-12) only name 'overlap' and 'unowned tracked paths ... shared-path rule' -- 'reverse-coverage' and 'ownership-digest' checks have no matching acceptance criterion anywhere in acceptance-tests.md, and unlike other compound ACs (AC-015, AC-018, AC-021, AC-027, AC-029) the table's Coverage note does not expand AC-005/AC-006 to name these two branches. Separately, REQ-008 (requirements.md:98-106) states verification 'shall reject a mixed transition ... or where required enforcement is activated before the selected Pack and resolver evidence are available'; AC-015 (acceptance-tests.md:21) covers only the first clause ('layout-only and enforcement-only'), leaving the second rejection condition (premature required-enforcement activation absent Pack/resolver evidence) without a matching AC. A task author implementing TEST-005/TEST-006 or TEST-014/TEST-015 from the AC table alone would not know these four named sub-checks/branches need independent test coverage, risking they ship unverified. This is a Phase-1 AC-completeness gap, squarely this gate's traceability duty, not a design or implementation choice; it is Major because it is a missing observable acceptance criterion for named requirement sub-clauses rather than a contradiction or missing safety/approval boundary.

Every row in acceptance-tests.md states an external, checkable oracle (schema acceptance of an exact tuple, fixture equality against a dated OQ ruling, zero-count ownership assertions, presence of named evidence fields, CI matrix execution) rather than unmeasured intent.

requirements.md:158-164 lists five explicit non-goals (no live sdd/ file during bootstrap, no later Packs, no Registry/resolver/Manifest/approval-model replacement, no new UI/CI, no self-approval of the spec/task/sidecar/WFI). The Transferred Backlog section (requirements.md:384-406) explicitly disclaims membership in this epic's REQ/AC set, reinforcing rather than eroding the boundary.

Security Boundaries (requirements.md:249-255), the ADR-0019-grounded approval/HMAC constraints in REQ-001/REQ-009/OQ-004, the atomic-migration constraint in REQ-008, and the cross-platform/CI-preservation constraint in REQ-012/AC-022-024 make data, compatibility, security, migration, and approval boundaries explicit and file-anchored.

Each of the four Risks (requirements.md:377-382) maps to a concrete validation surface: over-broad ownership -> AC-005/AC-006; premature required-enforcement deadlock -> the OQ-003 promotion criteria feeding AC-012/AC-013; Pack duplication -> AC-009 plus OQ-006's composition-by-reference design; unusable rollback governance -> OQ-004's cardinality rule feeding AC-016/AC-017/AC-018.
